name: Resilience
definition: You quickly adapt to changing circumstances; you make tough decisions without agonizing or long delay; you embrace a hard challenge.

rows.situation: Circumstances change in the middle of the work
rows.under: Keeps executing the old plan, or freezes until someone else redraws it.
rows.justRight: Changes the plan to fit what is true now, tells the people affected, and keeps moving.
rows.over: Changes direction every time a new fact appears, and nobody can build on yesterday's decision.

rows.situation: A decision that will not get more comfortable by waiting
rows.under: Agonizes in meetings until the choice is made for you.
rows.justRight: Makes the call, says what you are giving up, and moves.
rows.over: Decides before you have the facts that were already available, and calls the rush resilience.

rows.situation: Work that is genuinely hard and worth doing
rows.under: Looks for a version that will not stretch anyone.
rows.justRight: Takes the hard version, breaks it into the next step, and stays with it.
rows.over: Chooses the hardest framing even when a simpler one would produce the same result.

rows.under: Drops the effort, or pretends it did not happen.
rows.justRight: Names what failed, keeps what still works, and takes the next step the same week.
rows.over: Treats recovery as a performance and will not let the team sit with what actually broke.

rows.situation: A short-term bump in an approach that is still right
rows.under: Abandons it at the first bad week.
rows.justRight: Stays with it through the bump, and sets a point where you will reconsider if the bump is actually a wall.
rows.over: Calls every wall a bump and will not reconsider.
